Cyan Clayworks: Courses - Cyan Clayworks Skip to content Our courses run throughout the year; taster classes, daytime and evening courses running over several weeks, and one/two day workshops. The taster sessions are ideal for complete beginners who would like to try one or two techniques. Absolutely no prior experience needed! We often run specialist one or two day workshops on Saturdays. These may focus on wheelthrowing and handbuilding, or monoprinting for example, allowing students to build their confidence in a particular area. We finish and fire your pieces ready to collect at a later date. The longer courses are usually suitable for beginners and/or those with some prior experience, and we run occasional intermediate level courses. Students will be able to try a wide range of techniques and find which ones that suit them best. For those who’ve worked with clay before we can go into more depth at the different stages of making; help you with creative decision-making, thinking about the relationship between the form and surface and much more. Depending on the individual course, the focus can be on different areas of ceramics, such as functional pots, coilbuilding, slabbuilding and surface decoration using slips and glazes. All of our courses have strictly limited numbers, and usually both of us are teaching to give everyone more input. Fiona specialises in handbuilding and the surface; Chris mainly in throwing and functional pots. All materials, use of tools/equipment and firings are included. Everything is prepped for you in advance and we have a range of coloured slips and glazes mixed by ourselves. Our approach to teaching is fairly hands-on and supportive, but without being too prescriptive – you can choose what you make. Each technique is demonstrated by us at the start of the class, and we can point you in the direction of other relevant artists and makers as appropriate for inspiration. We have a contemporary approach to ceramics, but also have a broad knowledge of its history. Cyan Clayworks is a ‘working’ studio where we both create and sell ceramics; you can look at and handle our work in the shop space, and often see pieces in progress. There are lots of books and journals in the studio for inspiration too. Both of us have trained in ceramics to post-graduate level, have been working professionally since the 1990s, and are highly committed to this creative field, and so we have a lot to offer our students in a friendly environment. We are occasionally asked if we offer any discounts for students or retirees. Unfortunately as we are a small non-profit studio we are unable to offer discounts- we keep our prices as low as they can be. Additionally we are not able to accommodate those under 16 or those with complex support needs; for health & safety and insurance reasons. Bird Box Building £25 Visit Green Keepers Barn - Number 4 on the map Experience the joy of woodworking in a condensed, stress-free environment! The Pentland Group invites you into the Greenkeepers workshop for a fun, wood work taster session. Build your own bird box. We have taken care of all the measuring and heavy sawing so you can get straight to the best parts: building and decorating. You will piece together the pre-cut sides, front, and back before selecting your favorite roof style—options include rustic larch or traditional felt. The session is wonderfully hands-on: you will start by blending your favourite wool colours, then layer them into a unique pattern on a bamboo mat. Next comes the magic—using warm water and skin-friendly olive soap, you will roll and agitate the wool until the fibres interlock perfectly. You’ll leave the session with a gorgeous 20cm x 20cm felted artwork to take home and display. Embroidery £10 Visit The May - Number 10 on the map Looking for a quick spark of creativity? This introductory class is perfect for complete beginners, families, and anyone looking to try something new in a relaxed, supportive environment. During the session, you will use a hot glue gun to "sketch" a small, raised design directly onto your fabric. Once set, you will use colorful embroidery thread to sew over your glue outline, creating a vibrant, puffed-out 3D masterpiece. Using dried herbs carefully collected from our very own grounds, we will guide you through an immersive tasting experience. You’ll sip and discover the unique qualities of classic blends like soothing chamomile, vibrant rose, and nutrient-rich nettle. Alongside the tasting, you will receive beautifully illustrated information leaflets packed with facts on each plant. Welcome Brain: Workshops and Training | Foster Inclusivity Now — Welcome Brain Consulting 0 Neurodiversity First Responder Training Every organisation has first aiders and, increasingly, mental health first aiders. Now it’s time to ensure someone is equipped to respond when a neurodivergent colleague, student, or customer is in distress.Our CPD-Certified Neurodiversity First Responder online training course provides participants with practical tools to recognise early signs of overwhelm, respond calmly and inclusively, and restore psychological safety. By the end of the day, delegates are ready to step into a designated “first responder” role, providing support with dignity when it’s needed most. View fullsize What’s covered:Understanding the role and responsibilities of a Neurodiversity First Responder.Spotting triggers and early warning signs of distress.Safe, respectful communication strategies that protect autonomy.Role play and feedback to practise real-time responses.Strategies for restoring trust and dignity after a crisis. This course is perfect for anyone in an organisation who may be the first point of contact when a colleague, student, or customer is in distress — from HR and line managers to teachers, front-of-house teams, and event staff. No prior knowledge is required; just a commitment to creating safer, more inclusive environments.Format: The online training is delivered as a full-day, CPD-certified interactive workshop. Participants learn core principles through short presentations, then work through case studies, small-group discussions, and structured role plays to cement their skills. Everyone who completes the day is certified by Welcome Brain as a Neurodiversity First Responder, giving them a recognised role within their organisation. The course is led by Dr. Claire Renfrew, a Chartered Psychologist and sector expert with extensive experience supporting neurodivergent individuals in professional environments. Fresh Stat: Events - Fresh Start EVENTS Help us by taking part in a challenge There are lots of different events you can organise or take part in to help support our work. Whether you are looking to take part in a physical challenge or do something you enjoy socially whilst raising funds for your favourite charity, there are many different ways you can raise funds and awareness for Fresh Start. Run the Edinburgh marathon, take part in the Scottish 5k or 10k, get grubby at Tough Mudder, get sponsored to climb a mountain, hold a bake sale, do a sponsored silence, take part in a game-a-thon, the ideas are endless and we would love to hear yours! You can even run your own event! Every little helps and we would love to support you in running your own fundraiser for Fresh Start, whether that’s providing promotional materials for a coffee morning, bake sale, or crafting evening, to something bigger! Check out some great ideas of how you can raise funds in your own unique way! We would love you to choose Fresh Start for any event you are taking part in and can support you in the sponsorship process and promote your efforts and progress through our social media channels if you wish. You can download our sponsorship form, with Gift Aid declaration here.
